title: I am, I have
why: Two verbs carry half of everyday Czech: být (to be) and mít (to have). Their endings work like Turkish personal endings.

bridge.title: Personal endings, like Turkish

rows.note: Vaktim yok. ne- sticks to the verb like -me-

bridge.note: Like Turkish, Czech usually drops 'I' and 'you'. The verb ending already says who.

dialog.cz: Ne, jsem tady rok. Jsem z Turecka.
dialog.en: No, I've been here a year. I'm from Turkey.
Do you have time for a coffee?
Not now. I have a meeting.

pattern.en: I don't have ___. čas, kartu, klíč.

silly.en: I'm not a bear. I'm a roll.
The cat has no time. She has a meeting.

postcard.title: Jára Cimrman
postcard.text: The greatest Czech genius never existed. Fictional inventor Jára Cimrman nearly won a national TV poll of the greatest Czechs.
